title: Faithfully flat descent of locally Koszul-regular ideals
statement: Let $A,B$ be commutative rings and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal and let $IB$ be the ideal of $B$ generated by $\varphi(I)$. Assume that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset B$ containing $IB$ there are $g\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ and a finite Koszul-regular sequence in $B_g$ generating $(IB)B_g$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence, def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Then for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ containing $I$ there are $h\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ and a finite Koszul-regular sequence in $A_h$ generating $IA_h$. Empty sequences and zero rings are allowed. No Noetherian or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 068N (lemma-flat-descent-regular-ideal), Koszul-regular case, with definition-regular-ideal (Tag 07CV) expanded.

proof.text: Put $J=IB$. For each prime containing $J$, choose a good principal neighbourhood $D(g)$ from the hypothesis. These opens, together with $D(t)$ for all $t\in J$, cover $\operatorname{Spec}B$: a prime outside $V(J)$ omits some $t\in J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], a finite subfamily covers and its elements generate one. On a good $D(g)$ the ideal $J_g$ has finitely many given generators; on $D(t)$ with $t\in J$, it is the unit ideal, generated by $1$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-of-localization-span], applied to the $B$-module $J$, makes $J$ finitely generated. This also handles $J=B$ and the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 068N, first paragraph; Tag 07CW (lemma-quasi-regular-ideal-finite), finite principal-cover argument; Algebra Tags 00E0, 00E8, 00EO

proof.text: For each member of a finite generating family of $J$, its membership in $IB$ expresses it as a finite sum $\sum b_j\varphi(x_j)$ with $x_j\in I$. Collect the finitely many $x_j$, and let $I_0\subseteq I$ be their generated ideal. These expressions give $I_0B=IB$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] to both $I_0$ and $I$ gives $I_0=\varphi^{-1}(I_0B)=\varphi^{-1}(IB)=I$. In particular $I$ is finitely generated, and its quotient $M=I/I^2$ is a finite $A/I$-module, generated by the classes of these same elements.

source.place: Tag 068N, first paragraph, descent of finiteness; Algebra Tag 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective), ideal contraction

proof.text: The good $g$ alone give a cover of $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$; choose a finite subcover by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact]. On each such localization, the specified Koszul-regular generators give a finite free conormal module $J_g/J_g^2$, by [lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis]. Since $B\to B_g$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-cotangent-flat-base-change-ring] identifies this module with $(J/J^2)_g$, with its canonical $B_g/J_g$-action. The residue classes of the selected $g$ generate one in $B/J$, by the cover criterion. Apply [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-projective] over $B/J$ to conclude that $J/J^2$ is finite projective. The empty cover over a zero quotient causes no exception.

source.place: Tag 068N, first paragraph; Tag 08RK (lemma-quasi-regular-ideal-finite-projective); Tags 0CEM, 062I, and Algebra Tag 00NX

proof.text: The map $A/I\to B/J$ is faithfully flat directly from [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Indeed, for any $A/I$-module $N$, the mutually inverse balanced maps $B\otimes_A N\rightleftarrows(B/J)\otimes_{A/I}N$ are $b\otimes n\mapsto\bar b\otimes n$ and $\bar b\otimes n\mapsto b\otimes n$. The second is independent of the lift because $J$ is generated by $\varphi(I)$ and $IN=0$. These identifications commute with all maps in an exactness test. Hence the equivalence of exactness before and after tensoring with $B$ supplies precisely the equivalence for $B/J$.

source.place: Tag 068N, first paragraph, faithfully flat quotient base change; Algebra Tag 00HB (definition-flat)

proof.text: As $A\to B$ is flat, [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-cotangent-flat-base-change-ring] gives $M\otimes_A B\cong J/J^2$. The balanced maps in the preceding step identify its left side with $M\otimes_{A/I}(B/J)$. Interchanging the two tensor factors, apply [lem-trf-local-projective-faithfully-flat-descent] to the faithfully flat map $A/I\to B/J$ and the module $M$. Step 3 verifies its projectivity hypothesis upstairs. Thus $M$ is projective, and step 2 already gives its finite generation.

source.place: Tag 068N, first paragraph, descent of finite projectivity; Algebra Tag 05A9 (theorem-ffdescent-projectivity)

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free] over $A/I$ to $M$ at $\mathfrak p/I$. Lift the resulting element to $f\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$. Then $M_f$ has a basis of some finite size $r$ over $(A/I)_f$. Localization is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], and [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-cotangent-flat-base-change-ring] identifies $M_f$ with $I_f/I_f^2$. Choose lifts $a_1,\ldots,a_r\in I_f$ of that basis. This is possible because $I_f\to I_f/I_f^2$ is a quotient map. In particular $I_f=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)+I_f^2$.

Set $C=I_f/(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$. It is finite because $I$ is finite, and the last equality of step 6 says $I_fC=C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-one-plus-ideal-annihilator] there is $u\in1+I_f$ annihilating $C$. Write $u=v/f^n$ with $v\in A$. Since $u$ has residue $1$ modulo $I_f$, it lies outside $\mathfrak p A_f$, so $v\notin\mathfrak p$. Put $h=fv\notin\mathfrak p$ and $R=A_h=(A_f)_u$; the equality of these localizations follows since $f$ is already inverted and inverting $u$ is inverting $v$. Annihilation by $u$ gives $I R=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)R$: explicitly $u x\in(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ for each $x\in I_f$, and $x=u^{-1}(ux)$ after localization. The classes of the $a_i$ still give a basis of $IR/(IR)^2$, by localizing the basis isomorphism and its inverse.

Put $S=B_{\varphi(h)}$ and $L=IS$. The map $R\to S$ is faithfully flat by the same exactness definition [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. For any $R$-module $N$, the balanced identification $B\otimes_A N\cong S\otimes_R N$ sends $b\otimes n$ to $(b/1)\otimes n$, with inverse $(b/\varphi(h)^k)\otimes n\mapsto b\otimes h^{-k}n$. It is natural in $N$, so the original exactness equivalence is the one needed over $R$. In particular $R\to S$ is flat. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-cotangent-flat-base-change-ring] identifies $(IR/(IR)^2)\otimes_R S$ with $L/L^2$; hence the images of $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ form a basis of the latter over $S/L$.

For each prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ containing $L$, contract it to $B$ and take a good $g\in B$ outside that contracted prime from the original hypothesis. Write $\gamma=g/1\in S$. The given Koszul-regular sequence $c_1,\ldots,c_s$ in $B_g$ generates $JB_g$; its images generate $LS_\gamma$. The map $B_g\to S_\gamma$ is localization at the image of $\varphi(h)$, thus flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. Consequently [lem-sc-koszul-regular-flat-base-change] makes the image tuple Koszul-regular in $S_\gamma$. Also $\gamma\notin\mathfrak q$, so this gives good principal neighbourhoods covering $V(L)$.

On one such $S_\gamma$, [lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis] makes the classes of $c_1,\ldots,c_s$ a basis of $LS_\gamma/(LS_\gamma)^2$. By step 8, localization and [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-cotangent-flat-base-change-ring] (using [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]), the classes of the $a_i$ are another basis of this same module. The chosen $\mathfrak q$ gives a prime of $S_\gamma/LS_\gamma$. Reducing both basis isomorphisms further to the field of fractions of the quotient by that prime gives a vector space with bases of cardinalities $r$ and $s$, hence $r=s$. Both tuples generate $LS_\gamma$. Now [lem-sfb-koszul-equal-length-generators] applies, proving that the images of $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ in $S_\gamma$ are Koszul-regular. This explains the length hypothesis that cannot be dropped from that cited lemma.

source.place: Tag 068N, Koszul-regular paragraph; Tag 066A (lemma-independence-of-generators), part (3), including verification of equal lengths

proof.text: Let $K=K_\bullet(S,a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ and $n>0$. For a good $\gamma$ as in steps 9--10, [lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso] identifies $K\otimes_S S_\gamma$ with the Koszul complex of the images, so its $n$-th homology is zero. To apply [lem-pc-flat-tensor-complex-cohom] literally, reindex $K$ as the bounded cochain complex $C^{-j}=K_j$ for $0\leq j\leq r$, zero elsewhere, with $d_C^{-j}=d_{K,j}$. Then $H^{-n}(C)=H_n(K)$ and the same equalities hold after tensoring. Since $S_\gamma$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], that cited comparison gives $(H_n(K))_\gamma=0$.

Write $H=H_n(K)$. The homotopy of [lem-k3-koszul-generator-homotopy] shows that each $a_i$ kills $H$: for a cycle $z$, its homotopy equation gives $a_i z=d(h_i z)$, so its class is zero. Hence $H_{a_i}=0$ (an invertible element cannot annihilate a nonzero module). The good $D(\gamma)$ and the finitely many $D(a_i)$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}S$: the former cover $V(L)$ and a prime outside $V(L)$ omits one generator $a_i$ of $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], select a finite subcover whose elements generate one. Step 11 gives $H_\gamma=0$ on its good members, and the homotopy gives zero on its other members. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localized-span-eq-zero] to each $x\in H$, obtaining $x=0$. Thus $H_n(K)=0$ for every $n>0$.

By [lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso], the scalar extension of $K_\bullet(R,a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ to $S$ is $K$. Step 12 makes its differential triples exact in all positive degrees. Faithful flatness in the precise exactness-reflection form of [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], established for $R\to S$ in step 8, implies exactness of the original triples. Thus the tuple in $R=A_h$ is Koszul-regular by [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Step 7 gives its generation of $IA_h$ and $h\notin\mathfrak p$. Since $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$ was arbitrary, this proves the assertion. For $r=0$, $IA_h=0$ and the Koszul complex is concentrated in degree zero, so all the arguments still apply. If $I=A$ or $A=0$, there are no primes in $V(I)$ and the conclusion is vacuous.

tool_uses.why: The conormal classes of a Koszul-regular generating tuple are a basis, used on good charts and to compare lengths; a general commutative-algebra input absent from this unit.
Turns the finite principal conormal free cover over B/J into finite projectivity; no competing cover criterion in this unit.
Descends projectivity of I/I^2 over the faithfully flat quotient map; a generic module theorem, not a replacement for a unit step.
Produces a principal neighbourhood on which the descended finite projective conormal is free.
Preserves the given good generators when restricting a B chart to B_h; only the flat ascent assertion is taken.
Compares homology with principal localization after explicitly reindexing the finite Koszul chain complex as a bounded cochain complex.
Supplies an actual contraction; its equation is applied to cycles to prove annihilation, not an unstated homology theorem.
Identifies the actual scalar-extended Koszul complex with that on the image tuple, used for localization and exactness reflection.

lean.statement: theorem locally_koszulRegular_of_faithfullyFlat {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B] (I : Ideal A) (hlocal : ∀ q : Ideal B, q.IsPrime → I.map (algebraMap A B) ≤ q → ∃ g : B, g ∉ q ∧ ∃ r : ℕ, ∃ f : Fin r → Localization.Away g, RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f ∧ Ideal.span (Set.range f) = (I.map (algebraMap A B)).map (algebraMap B (Localization.Away g))) : ∀ p : Ideal A, p.IsPrime → I ≤ p → ∃ h : A, h ∉ p ∧ ∃ r : ℕ, ∃ f : Fin r → Localization.Away h, RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f ∧ Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I.map (algebraMap A (Localization.Away h))
